findings.produced: GuardrailRegistry::disable_all / GuardrailRegistry::enable_all (runtime kill-switch pair documented in master spec §Stage 5)
findings.consumer_location: zero call sites anywhere in src/, tests/, interfaces/, desktop/. The orchestrator's wiring at src/bin/aleph-server/commands/start/orchestrator_init.rs:573 builds the registry and passes it via HarnessDeps.guardrails — no code path ever flips the kill-switch.
findings.rationale: Two viable resolutions: (a) CONNECT — add a `gateway.guardrails.disable` admin RPC + corresponding Panel UI button so operators can flip the switch from a dashboard (this was the original spec intent). Without a UI hook, the switch is unreachable from any runtime state. (b) CUT — delete both methods, drop the AtomicBool field, simplify the four `evaluate_*` short-circuits. Recommend DECIDE: the spec intent is real, but no commit has landed the RPC. Painless-wire heuristic argues CUT (no production pain observed; the registry defaults to enabled and operators who hit a false-positive block currently have no recovery path besides restart). The decision should weigh: is a runtime kill-switch worth the surface it adds (admin RPC, Panel toggle, audit-log integration)? Or do we keep the build-time [guardrails].enabled switch as the only control?
findings.residual_risk: If kept dormant: an operator who hits a false-positive block from PiiSecretsGuardrail has no recovery path; the only options are restart with [guardrails].enabled = false (rebuild) or edit the [secrets_config].custom_leak_patterns list. CUTTING is safe if [guardrails].enabled remains the only control.

findings.produced: GuardrailDecision::is_allow / is_block / is_sanitize / is_warn (4 pub const fn accessors)
findings.consumer_location: Only used in #[cfg(test)] blocks: src/guardrails/decision.rs:92-126 (own unit tests), src/guardrails/tests/{registry.rs,input.rs,output.rs,bench.rs} (counted 21 test-call sites). Zero production callers — the live code uses match on the enum variants directly (registry.rs:96-122, 257-281, 286-309; harness/agent/think.rs:349-365, 849-855, 1212-1219, 1293-1306).
findings.rationale: Pure test-only API. Production callers all `match` on the enum directly (which is what #[non_exhaustive] is meant to allow — destructuring the variant gets the inner data). Demoting all four to pub(crate) would break no production code (tests live in src/guardrails/tests/ which can still access pub(crate) via `mod tests` inside mod.rs). Alternatively, delete and inline the test assertions. Recommend demoting to pub(crate) — it's a five-character change per method and preserves the test ergonomics.
findings.residual_risk: Trivial: no production callers; tests still compile.
